[element-kwd-group]
=== `<kwd-group>` Keyword Group

Container element for one set of keywords (<<element-kwd,`<kwd>`>>, <<element-nested-kwd,`<nested-kwd>`>>, or <<element-compound-kwd,`<compound-kwd>`>>) used to describe a document. A keyword records one specific term, key phrase, abbreviation, taxonomic structure, or other expression that is found within the text of a standards document, or implied (broader, narrower, etc.) from terms found within this text.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Language in Keywords

A standard may take multiple sets of keywords, with the <<attribute-kwd-group-type,`@kwd-group-type`>>, <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>, or <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>> attributes used to discriminate between them. The keyword elements (<<element-kwd,`<kwd>`>>, <<element-nested-kwd,`<nested-kwd>`>>, or <<element-compound-kwd,`<compound-kwd>`>>) do not take the <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>> attribute; that is reserved for the `<kwd-group>` element. This means that keywords must be sorted by language and entered in language groups.
#### Vocabulary Attributes

Two vocabulary attributes can be used to link a keyword group to a controlled vocabulary: <<attribute-vocab,`@vocab`>> — This attribute holds the name of a controlled or generic (uncontrolled) vocabulary, taxonomy, ontology, database, thesaurus, etc. that is the source of the keywords in the group, for example, “`CRediT`”, “`inspec`”, “`structural engineering`”, or “`VWL`”. In cases where there is no named vocabulary, the <<attribute-vocab,`@vocab`>> attribute should be set to “`uncontrolled`”. <<attribute-vocab-identifier,`@vocab-identifier`>> — This attribute holds a unique identifier and possible pointer to the named vocabulary (typically a URI or DOI reference).
#### Keyword Group Type

The <<attribute-kwd-group-type,`@kwd-group-type`>> attribute most commonly names an uncontrolled vocabulary source of the keywords, such as “`chemical engineering`”, “`author-generated`”, or “`working-group-generated`”. But <<attribute-kwd-group-type,`@kwd-group-type`>> has also been used to record the type of keywords, for example, “`hierarchical`” for keywords that are grouped into a hierarchy, “`abbreviations`” for keywords that contain an abbreviation and its expansion, or “`code`” for keywords that contain a code and its text but where the source of the codes is unknown.
#### Historical Note

Older documents, coded before NISO STS added the vocabulary attributes, may have used <<attribute-kwd-group-type,`@kwd-group-type`>> to name the vocabulary source. Going forward, this information should be recorded using the vocabulary attributes.
##### Vocabulary Attributes Best Practice

If the keywords in a `<kwd-group>` come from a controlled vocabulary, taxonomy, ontology, database, term list, index, or similar formally defined term source, the <<attribute-vocab,`@vocab`>> attribute (and if possible, the <<attribute-vocab-identifier,`@vocab-identifier`>> attribute) should be used on the `<kwd-group>` element to name the source. If there is a keyword-specific identifier in this source of terms, then also use the <<attribute-vocab-term,`@vocab-term`>> and <<attribute-vocab-term-identifier,`@vocab-term-identifier`>> on the keyword element (<<element-kwd,`<kwd>`>>, <<element-nested-kwd,`<nested-kwd>`>>, or <<element-compound-kwd,`<compound-kwd>`>>), if possible.
If the keywords come from, or are specific to, a field of study that can be named (particularly where different fields might define the same term differently), name the field of study in the <<attribute-kwd-group-type,`@kwd-group-type`>> attribute (“`structural engineering`”, “`mechanical engineering`”, “`bird watching`”). Such terms are typically, but not always, informally defined.
If the keyword terms are uncontrolled, either omit the <<attribute-vocab,`@vocab`>> attribute on `<kwd-group>` element or use the value “`uncontrolled`”.

#### Related Elements

*Keywords vs Subjects Terms:* Subject terms (collected within a <<element-subj-group,`<subj-group>`>> element) name broad classifications, categories, topics, or themes that describe or classify a standard. Keywords (collected within a <<element-kwd-group,`<kwd-group>`>> element) contain words from the narrative text or words (such as broader and narrower terms) related to that text.

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-app-group,`<app-group>`>>, <<element-chem-struct-wrap,`<chem-struct-wrap>`>>, <<element-disp-formula,`<disp-formula>`>>, <<element-disp-formula-group,`<disp-formula-group>`>>, <<element-fig,`<fig>`>>, <<element-fig-group,`<fig-group>`>>, <<element-graphic,`<graphic>`>>, <<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>>, <<element-media,`<media>`>>, <<element-nat-meta,`<nat-meta>`>>, <<element-reg-meta,`<reg-meta>`>>, <<element-sec-meta,`<sec-meta>`>>, <<element-statement,`<statement>`>>, <<element-std-doc-meta,`<std-doc-meta>`>>, <<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>>, <<element-supplementary-material,`<supplementary-material>`>>, <<element-table-wrap,`<table-wrap>`>>, <<element-table-wrap-group,`<table-wrap-group>`>>
#### Description

The following, in order: <<element-editing-instruction,`<editing-instruction>`>> <<element-editing-instruction,Editing Instruction>>, zero or more <<element-label,`<label>`>> <<element-label,Label of a Figure, Reference, Etc.>>, zero or one <<element-title,`<title>`>> <<element-title,Title>>, zero or one One or more of any of: <<element-kwd,`<kwd>`>> <<element-kwd,Keyword>> <<element-compound-kwd,`<compound-kwd>`>> <<element-compound-kwd,Compound Keyword>> <<element-nested-kwd,`<nested-kwd>`>> <<element-nested-kwd,Nested Keyword>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  kwd-group    %kwd-group-model;                            >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

((editing-instruction)*, label?, title?, (kwd | compound-kwd | nested-kwd)+)

#### Tagged Samples

#### INSPEC keywords added by SDO

[source,xml]
....
...
<kwd-group kwd-group-type="INSPEC" originator="IEEE">
 <kwd>social networking (online)</kwd>
 <kwd>buyer&#x0027;s guides</kwd>
 <kwd>electronic commerce</kwd>
</kwd-group> 

<kwd-group kwd-group-type="InspecFree" originator="IEEE">
 <kwd>whiz list</kwd>
 <kwd>social networking sites</kwd>
 <kwd>online purchase</kwd>
 <kwd>e-commerce portals</kwd>
 <kwd>Web site users</kwd>
 <kwd>marketing strategy</kwd>
</kwd-group>
...
....
